original_question: For families of graded Artinian Gorenstein algebras that fail the weak Lefschetz property, determine the number of parts in their generic linear Jordan types. More generally, for a graded Artinian Gorenstein algebra that fails the strong Lefschetz property, determine its generic linear Jordan type.
target_in_paper: Section 5, Question 5.7 (under the subsection "Jordan type of graded Artinian Gorenstein algebras").
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official target very closely: it has the correct class of algebras (graded Artinian Gorenstein), the correct invariant (generic linear Jordan type), and the exact two-level scope of the paper's formulation—first the number of parts for WLP-failure families, then the full generic linear Jordan type for SLP-failure algebras. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))
missing_details: Specify the ambient field k; in Section 5 the setup is over an arbitrary field, unlike Section 2 where characteristic-zero hypotheses are imposed. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))

Make explicit that one is in the graded setting with a degree-one piece A_1 and a generic linear form ℓ ∈ A_1; this is how the paper defines the generic linear Jordan type. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))
Define the operator whose Jordan type is being asked for: the multiplication map m_ℓ:A→A, a↦ℓa, with A viewed as a module over itself. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))
State that m_ℓ is nilpotent because A is Artinian, so its Jordan type is a finite partition of dim_k A. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))

Clarify that the first clause refers to the families of graded Artinian Gorenstein algebras already discussed nearby as known WLP-failure families, rather than broadening the question to an unrelated classification problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))
Spell out that the first clause asks only for the number of Jordan blocks, whereas the second asks for the entire Jordan partition. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))

If the question is to be fully stand-alone, replace the bare phrase "generic linear Jordan type" by its definition in terms of Jordan blocks of multiplication by a generic linear form. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))
refined_question: Let k be a field and let A = ⊕_{i=0}^d A_i be a standard graded Artinian Gorenstein k-algebra. For a generic linear form ℓ ∈ A_1, let P_{A,ℓ} denote the Jordan partition of the nilpotent multiplication map m_ℓ:A→A, a↦ℓa. For the known families of graded Artinian Gorenstein algebras that fail the weak Lefschetz property, determine the number of parts of P_{A,ℓ}. More generally, if A fails the strong Lefschetz property, determine the full generic linear Jordan type P_{A,ℓ}.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for a generic linear form ℓ ∈ A_1, determine the Jordan block decomposition of multiplication by ℓ on A; in the weak-Lefschetz-failure families, determine only the number of Jordan blocks.
justification: The draft is essentially the paper's Question 5.7 verbatim, so the intended target is the Jordan-type problem in Section 5 rather than an earlier conjecture or theorem. The immediately surrounding text supplies the missing stand-alone data: Jordan type is defined via multiplication by an element, the generic linear Jordan type is the Jordan type for a generic linear form, and the nearby discussion explains why the WLP half of the question asks only for the number of parts while the SLP half asks for the full partition. The same local context also frames the first sentence around already known WLP-failure families of graded Artinian Gorenstein algebras. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))
